description.narrative:
The GenACT Shaping AYSRHR through Unified Transformative Innovation (GenACT SAUTI) project strengthens youth leadership in shaping Tanzania’s next National Accelerated Investment Agenda for Adolescent Health and Well-being at a time of declining donor funding forAYSRHR. Led entirely by young people through the GenACT network, the project will equip youth advocates with SMART advocacy skills,policy and budget analysis tools, and platforms to engage government and other stakeholders. It will promote meaningful youth participation in NAIA II design and accountability processes while advancing innovative domestic financing models for Youth-Friendly Services, Comprehensive Sexuality Education, and Gender-Based Violence prevention and response. By positioning young people as credible policy actors and financing innovators, the project will contribute to more sustainable, locally owned, and youth-responsive AYSRHR systems in Tanzania.
Goal: To strengthen youth-led influence on Tanzania’s post-2025 NAIA by embedding meaningful adolescent and youth participation and advancing sustainable, innovative domestic financing for SRHR interventions amid declining donor support.
Objectives: Ensure GenACT youth members actively and credibly participate in the design of the next iteration of NAIA. Co-develop and advocate for innovative domestic financing models for AYSRHR (public budgets, insurance, local revenue, PPPs). Build strong SMART Advocacy skills among youth advocates.
Activities: Policy and budget analysis Member's Training <(>&<)> Advocacy Strategy Community dialogues Structured engagement with government Advocacy campaign

participating-org.narrative:
GenACT (Generation Action Africa) is a dynamic, inter-generational network of youth-led organizations, creative professionals, community champions, and change makers dedicated to improving the health, well-being, livelihoods, and rights of adolescents and young people across Tanzania and the African continent. We envision a society where adolescents and young people thrive supported by inclusive systems, youth-centered leadership, and equitable access to information and services.
GenACT operates through a youth-governed participatory structure made up of a Board of Directors, thematic working groups, a national secretariat, and regional representatives. Our work integrates Advocacy <(><<)>(><(>&<)><(><<)>)> Social accountability, Knowledge Management, and Capacity Building, with a strong emphasis on creative civic engagement, and community dialogues.
GenACT is built by young people, for young people. It operates through a participatory, youth-governed structure that brings together member organisations, a Board of Directors, thematic working groups, and a small but active Secretariat. GenACT is a network of over 40 organisations. Members are actively involved in shaping the network’s priorities, strategies, and actions. The Secretariat consists of nine young professionals, all under the age of 35, who coordinate daily operations and ensure strong collaboration across the network. They convene and support three main advocacy working groups: Health <(><<)>(><(>&<)><(><<)>)> Wellbeing, Youth Engagement <(><<)>(><(>&<)><(><<)>)> Rights, and Economic Justice. Through these spaces, young people lead the entire programme cycle from identifying issues and designing interventions to implementation, learning, and reflection. The Board also largely under 35, provides strategic oversight, ensuring the organisation remains firmly rooted in young people’s lived realities and aspirations.
